what: American Electric Power is a regulated electricity utility serving about 5.6 million customers across eleven states, and it owns one of the largest transmission networks in the United States.
customers: Households, businesses and industrial users in Texas, Ohio, Oklahoma, Indiana, Virginia and other states.
money: generating and selling electricity in states where it owns power plants
moving power over its wires, including its large transmission business
moat: A regulated monopoly over the wires in its territories, with rates set to recover costs plus an allowed return on investment.
risks: Debt of about $50 billion makes it sensitive to interest rates
Regulators in eleven states each decide what it can charge
Large new transmission projects can be delayed or denied
Storms and extreme weather damage the network
opportunities: Data centre demand in Ohio, Texas and Indiana is driving the fastest load growth in decades
Transmission investment is the highest-return part of its business
A large approved capital plan grows the base its earnings are calculated on
watch: Approved rate cases and signed data centre load agreements.
